findings.title: Continuation equality accepts a split inside an unclosed TeX argument

findings.evidence: The new continuation condition checks whitespace and a leading =/+/-, but does not check that each math span is independently closed. The reproduced invalid fraction fragments therefore receive exactly the same signature as the intact fraction. validate_text uses this equality as its math-preservation gate at edition.py:867; the new tests protect command boundaries and changed group tokens, but do not reject splitting a formula inside its still-open group.
findings.consequence: A malformed layout-only candidate can pass this shared mathematical-preservation comparison. The renderer handles each math span separately (render_lesson.js:73, throwOnError:false), so this equality is not evidence that the split retains a renderable formula. This is a concrete gate regression, not a defect in the current N42 row or an inherited answer/choice semantic finding.

Add a negative regression for the supplied split-fraction counterexample, without weakening the existing token/sign/command-boundary protections.
